Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in using natural salt-lake water directly as an electrolyte solvent, eliminating costly purification while enabling −50 °C operation. Combined with an alloy-coated Zn anode, it suppresses freezing and water activity, achieving 3200 h cycling and stable pouch cells. This offers a low-cost, scalable strategy for extreme-cold aqueous batteries.

💡 The novelty is a non-hybrid aqueous flow cell achieving 2.2 V open-circuit potential by passively sustaining a ~7-unit pH gradient across a single cation-exchange membrane, without oxygen or bipolar-membrane recovery.
